chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Makfūf, from ʿAmr al-Ahwāzī, who said:
Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) showed him to me and said: “This is your Master.”

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: Abū Muḥammad, the teknonym of Imam al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام) in this report
key_terms.أَرَانِيهِ: showed him to me; indicating direct presentation or identification
key_terms.صَاحِبُكُمْ: your Master; referring to the recognized Imam
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: peace be upon him; honorific used for the Imam
key_terms.هَذَا: this one; a direct demonstrative identification

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate that Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) identified the Imam to his companions?
ai.summary: This report states that Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) personally showed the awaited figure to the narrator and identified him as their Master. The narration is significant in Shia tradition as a testimony concerning recognition of the Imam and affirmation of his identity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Makfouf, from Amro Al Ahwazy who said,
‘Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) showed him<sup>asws</sup> to me and said: ‘This is your Master<sup>asws</sup>’’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Makfuf from ‘Amr al-Ahwazi who has said the following.
“Abu Muhammad (a.s.) showed him (the twelfth Imam (a.s.) to me and said, “This will be your master (Leader with Divine Authority).”
